title: Truthy and falsy values
learningObjectives: Explain truthy and falsy values and use JavaScript values and operators predictably.

understand.concept: JavaScript conditions convert values to booleans. Falsy values include false, 0, -0, 0n, empty string, null, undefined, and NaN. Most other values, including empty arrays and empty objects, are truthy.
understand.whyItMatters: Truthiness affects if statements, logical operators, and defaulting patterns. Do not assume an empty array or object is falsy, and use explicit comparisons when the domain meaning requires them.
understand.analogy: A truthy value passes a condition check; a falsy value behaves like false in a boolean context.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript coercion, equality, and reference semantics follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The empty array and empty object convert to true, while zero, empty string, null, and undefined convert to false.

examples.explanation: The empty array and empty object convert to true, while zero, empty string, null, and undefined convert to false.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the values and results described.

practise.guidedTask: Test common falsy values and compare them with an empty array and empty object. Explain why each result matters in conditions.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program using the concept with realistic values. Predict the output before running it and explain any surprising result.
hints: Inspect both value and typeof when needed.
Use explicit conversion and validate its result.
Avoid relying on implicit coercion in security-sensitive logic.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Truthy and falsy values</title></head><body>
<script>const values=[0,'',null,undefined,[],{}];values.forEach(value=>console.log(value,Boolean(value)));</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Is an empty array falsy in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: All objects, including empty arrays, are truthy.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to understand a value conversion?
options: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.answer: Inspect the original value, converted value, and conversion result
questions.explanation: Explicitly checking conversion results prevents invalid values from silently entering later calculations.
